title: console-observability-triage-scratchpad-emily-nguyen
content:
Console / Observability triage scratchpad - Emily Nguyen

Context: quick personal log while handling dashboard bugs and customer-reported issues. Mostly scratchy notes, queries, and todo items. Not polished.

2025-02-12 09:10 - kickoff
- Customer (AcmeCorp) reported missing panels and 502s when loading /console/dashboards/usage (INC-4721).
- Slack thread: #inc-4721 (linked above).
- First pass: reproduce in prod from my laptop (us-west).

Repro steps taken:
1) Hit console -> dashboards -> usage: observed 502 for first load, subsequent loads sometimes succeed but panels empty.
2) Opened Chrome devtools: several panel requests -> 502, one 200 but payload size 0.
3) Checked Grafana proxy logs (prod-grafana-01): spike of 502s around 08:58-09:05 UTC.
4) Checked service logs for dashboard-renderer: errors about upstream timeout to metrics-api.

Quick hypotheses:
- metrics-api latency spike causing renderer timeouts -> 502 bubbled to UI
- recent deploy to metrics-api (OPS-4879) might be related
- cache invalidation / bursting of DB reads when many customers load dashboards after maintenance window

Queries & checks to run (prometheus / p95 / logs)
- PromQL: rate(http_requests_total{job="metrics-api",status=~"5.."}[5m]) -> spike at 08:57
- histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="metrics-api"}[5m])) by (le)) -> p95 ~ 1.9s at spike (normal ~ 120ms)
- SQL (analytics DB): SELECT count(*) FROM dashboard_queries WHERE created_at > now() - interval '10 minutes' AND service = 'metrics-api'; -> burst of queries from renderer cluster

Notes from logs:
- metrics-api pod metrics-api-7f6cc had repeated warnings: "upstream read timeout after 30s"
- autoscaler did not scale quickly because HPA target based on CPU not request latency.

Temporary mitigations attempted:
- Rolled back metrics-api to previous revision (deployed 2025-02-11 21:00) -> immediate reduction in 5xx, UI loads improved for me locally.
- Flipped feature flag to route dashboard rendering to dedicated renderer pool for AcmeCorp while we investigate (feature flag: ff/dedicated-renderer-acmecorp)

Customer communication draft (send after morning stand):
"Hi Alex (AcmeCorp),
Thanks for the report — we saw the same issue and identified a latency spike in our metrics API that caused renderer timeouts and 502s in the console. We've rolled back a recent change and applied a temporary routing tweak to keep your dashboards on the dedicated renderer pool while we finish a root cause investigation. We'll follow up with a postmortem and next steps by EOD PT.
— Emily (Observability)"

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm rollback metrics across all regions (Riley)
- [ ] Add request-latency-based HPA experiment for metrics-api (ticket OPS-4922)
- [ ] Run load test against renderer+metrics-api combo to reproduce burst behavior (Maya)
- [ ] Add alert for sustained p95 > 1s on metrics-api (pager rule?)
- [ ] Draft postmortem skeleton (link to postmortem doc)

2025-02-13 11:40 - discovery after more data
- Looked at Canary and Dedicated capacity graphs in Console -> observed that dedicated renderer pool had higher concurrency but remained healthy.
- Root cause likely combination: recent change introduced occasionally blocking I/O on metrics-api (sync file op in rare code path) + HPA config that scales on CPU only.
- Action: open PR to remove blocking op (in progress, PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metrics-api/pull/238)

Notes on alert tuning (brain dump):
- Current alert: metrics-api_5xx_rate > 1% for 5m -> noisy during deploys and acceptable small blips.
- Suggest: new alert metrics-api_p95_latency > 1s for 3m with severity=page (only paging if region==prod and customer-facing dashboards impacted)
- Add mute window for deploys or estimate deploy windows from CI/Deploy metadata

Hand-off checklist (if I go offline):
- Current status: rollback applied, customer routed to ded-renderer, PR #238 pending review, load test scheduled 2025-02-14 02:00 UTC.
- Key contacts: Riley Park (SRE) - pager, Maya Singh (Renderer eng) - helping with load test, Alex (AcmeCorp) - customer contact.
- Where to look: Grafana dashboards -> Console -> Renderers (dash_id=console-renderers-01), Prometheus cluster: prometheus-prod, Kibana logs: logs-prod/_dash (query: "metrics-api" AND "upstream read timeout")

Scratch commands to re-run quickly:
- kubectl -n prod logs deploy/metrics-api --since=15m | grep "upstream read timeout"
- curl -v "https://console.redwood.com/api/dashboards/usage?org=acmecorp" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
- promql: increase(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job=\"metrics-api\"}[5m]) / increase(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job=\"metrics-api\"}[1h])

Loose thoughts / risks:
- If PR introduces CPU regressions we may see scaling oscillations - monitor HPA metrics closely.
- Need to make renderer routing by customer more automated so ops doesn't have to flip flags manually.

End notes (2025-02-14 08:22)
- PR merged 2025-02-13 20:12, deployed 2025-02-14 02:45 UTC. Verified p95 steady ~ 110ms after change.
- Re-evaluate whether to keep latency HPA (OPS-4922) or use SLO-based autoscaling (longer term).

-- Emily
